title.en: Volume 87: Treatise on the Western Qiang
title.raw: 卷八十七 西羌傳 Volume 87: Treatise on the Western Qiang

sentences.zh: 西羌之本，出自三苗，姜姓之别也。

translations.literal: The roots of the Western Qiang issue from the Three Miao; they are an offshoot of the Jiang surname.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Qiang trace their origins to the Three Miao and constitute a branch of the Jiang lineage.

sentences.zh: 其国近南岳。

translations.literal: Their country lay near the southern sacred peak.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands bordered the Southern Marchmount.

sentences.zh: 及舜流四凶，徙之三危，河关之西南羌地是也。

translations.literal: When Shun banished the Four Fiends and relocated them to Sanwei, the southwestern Qiang lands southwest of Heguan were those lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Shun exiled the Four Malefactors and removed them to Sanwei, the region was that southwestern Qiang territory southwest of Heguan.

sentences.zh: 滨于赐支，至乎河首，绵地千里。

translations.literal: They bordered on Zhizhi and reached to the river's head; the territory stretched a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Their domain ran along Zhizhi all the way to the river's source, spanning a thousand li of ground.

sentences.zh: 赐支者，《禹贡》所谓析支者也。

translations.literal: Zhizhi is what the "Tribute of Yu" calls Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi is the place the "Tribute of Yu" names Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 南接蜀、汉徼外蛮夷，西北接鄯善、车师诸国。

translations.literal: To the south they bordered the barbarians beyond Shu and Han; to the northwest they bordered the states of Shanshan, Jushi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Southward they met the tribes beyond Shu and Han; northwestward they adjoined Shanshan, Jushi, and the other oasis states.

sentences.zh: 所居无常，依随水草。

translations.literal: They had no fixed dwelling places and followed water and pasture.
translations.idiomatic: They did not live in one place for long; they moved with the grass and water.

sentences.zh: 地少五谷，以产牧为业。

translations.literal: The land had little of the five grains; they made their living by herding.
translations.idiomatic: Where grain was scarce, they lived chiefly by pastoralism.

sentences.zh: 其俗氏族无定，或以父名母姓为种号。

translations.literal: Their customs had no fixed clan names; some took their father's name and mother's surname as their tribal designation.
translations.idiomatic: Clan affiliation was fluid: some groups styled themselves from a father's name combined with a mother's surname.

sentences.zh: 十二世后，相与婚姻，父没则妻后母，兄亡则纳厘嫂，故国无鳏寡，种类繁炽。

translations.literal: After twelve generations they intermarried with one another; when the father died they married the stepmother, when an elder brother died they took in the widowed sister-in-law; hence the state had no widowers or widows, and the tribes multiplied vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve generations on they freely intermarried; a son could wed his father's widow and a younger brother his brother's widow, so few were left alone, and their kind grew thick on the ground.

sentences.zh: 不立君臣，无相长一，强则分种为酋豪，弱则为人附落，更相抄暴，以力为雄。

translations.literal: They did not establish lord and minister, nor any single overseer; when strong they split off into chieftains, when weak they attached themselves to others' camps, raiding one another in turn and making might the measure of leadership.
translations.idiomatic: They knew no formal ruler-subject order; the powerful broke away as chieftains, the weak became dependents of larger camps, and they pillaged each other ceaselessly, with raw strength deciding who led.

sentences.zh: 杀人偿死，无它禁令。

translations.literal: For killing a man one paid with one's life; there were no other prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Murder was repaid with death, and little else was forbidden by law.

sentences.zh: 其兵长在山谷，短于平地，不能持久，而果于触突，以战死为吉利，病终为不祥。

translations.literal: Their soldiers were strong in mountain valleys and weak on level ground; they could not fight long engagements, yet they were bold in sudden charges; they counted dying in battle auspicious and dying of illness inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: They fought best in the defiles and poorly on open plains, could not sustain long campaigns, yet rushed headlong into shock action; a battlefield death was lucky, while sickness was ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 堪耐寒苦，同之禽兽。

translations.literal: They could endure cold and hardship as beasts do.
translations.idiomatic: They bore cold and privation like wild creatures.

sentences.zh: 虽妇人产子，亦不避风雪。

translations.literal: Even when women gave birth they did not avoid wind and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Women gave birth without sheltering from wind or snow.

sentences.zh: 性坚刚勇猛，得西方金行之气焉。

translations.literal: Their nature was stubborn, fierce, and brave; they possessed the qi of the Metal phase of the west.
translations.idiomatic: They were hard, fierce, and courageous—said to embody the western Metal phase in temperament.

sentences.zh: 王政修则宾服，德教失则寇乱。

translations.literal: When royal government was well ordered they came as guests and submitted; when virtue and instruction failed they plundered and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Good governance brought them to court as tributaries; misrule turned them into raiders.

sentences.zh: 昔夏后氏太康失国，西夷背叛。

translations.literal: In ancient times the Xia House's Taikang lost the state, and the western Yi turned disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taikang of the Xia the throne was lost and the western Yi broke away.

sentences.zh: 及后相即位，乃征畎夷，七年然后来宾。

translations.literal: When later Xiang ascended the throne, he campaigned against the Quanyi, and only after seven years did they come as guests.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiang took the throne he attacked the Quanyi, and seven years passed before they arrived as suppliants.

sentences.zh: 至于后泄，始加爵命，由是服从。

translations.literal: Down to later Xie he first conferred ranks and commands, whereupon they obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the reign of Xie were titles and orders first granted, and from then on they submitted.

sentences.zh: 后桀之乱，畎夷入居邠、岐之间，成汤既兴，伐而攘之。

translations.literal: Amid the turmoil of later Jie the Quanyi moved in to dwell between Bin and Qi; when Cheng Tang rose, he attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Jie's chaos erupted the Quanyi settled between Bin and Qi until Cheng Tang's rise, when he struck them and cleared them out.

sentences.zh: 及殷室中衰，诸夷皆叛。

translations.literal: When the Yin house declined in its middle period, the various Yi all rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the mid-Yin decline every Yi group rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 至于武丁，征西戎、鬼方，三年乃克。

translations.literal: Down to Wuding he campaigned against the western Rong and Guifang, and only after three years did he subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuding the court campaigned against the western Rong and Guifang and needed three years to overcome them.

sentences.zh: 故其诗曰：“自彼氐羌，莫敢不来王。

translations.literal: Therefore the ode says: “From those Di and Qiang none dared not come to acknowledge the king.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the poem runs: “From those Di and Qiang tribes, none dared refuse to present themselves at court.

translations.literal: Closing double quotation mark concluding the verse cited above.
translations.idiomatic: The quotation from the classic ends at this closing mark.

sentences.zh: 及武乙暴虐，犬戎寇边，周古公逾梁山而避于岐下。

translations.literal: When Wuyi was cruel and violent, the Quanrong raided the border; Zhou's ancient lord crossed Mount Liang and took refuge below Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Under the tyrant Wuyi the Quanrong harried the frontier until the Zhou patriarch crossed Mount Liang and sheltered beneath Mount Qi.

sentences.zh: 及子季历，遂伐西落鬼戎。

translations.literal: Down to his son Jili, he then attacked the Xiluo Gui Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jili next campaigned against the Xiluo Gui Rong.

sentences.zh: 太丁之时，季历复伐燕京之戎，戎人大败周师。

translations.literal: In the time of Taiding, Jili again attacked the Yanjing Rong; the Rong badly defeated the Zhou army.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiding's reign Jili struck the Yanjing Rong again, and the Rong shattered the Zhou host.

sentences.zh: 后二年，周人克余无之戎，于是太丁命季历为牧师。

translations.literal: Two years later the Zhou people conquered the Yuwu Rong; thereupon Taiding ordered Jili to be herds instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on the Zhou crushed the Yuwu Rong, and Taiding appointed Jili pastoral superintendent.

sentences.zh: 自是之后，更伐始呼、翳徒之戎，皆克之。

translations.literal: After this they repeatedly attacked the Shihu and Yitu Rong and overcame them all.
translations.idiomatic: They went on to defeat the Shihu and Yitu Rong in successive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 乃文王为西伯，西有昆夷之患，北有猃狁之难，遂攘戎狄而戍之，莫不宾服。

translations.literal: Then King Wen became western lord; there was trouble with the Kunyi on the west and trouble with the Xianyun on the north; he therefore drove off the Rong and Di and garrisoned against them, and none failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen became overlord of the west he faced Kunyi in the west and Xianyun in the north; he pushed back Rong and Di, posted troops, and brought every side to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 乃率西戎，征殷之叛国以事纣。

translations.literal: He then led the western Rong to campaign against Yin rebel states in order to serve Zhouxin.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied the western Rong to strike Yin territories that had broken away, thereby serving King Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及武王伐商，羌、髳率师会于牧野。

translations.literal: When King Wu attacked Shang, the Qiang and Mao led their hosts to join at Muye.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu marched against Shang, the Qiang and Mao brought their forces to Muye.

sentences.zh: 至穆王时，戎狄不贡，王乃西征犬戎，获其五王，又得四白鹿，四白狼，王遂迁戎于太原。

translations.literal: Down to King Mu the Rong and Di ceased tribute; the king therefore campaigned west against the Quanrong, captured five of their kings, and also obtained four white deer and four white wolves; the king then moved the Rong to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under King Mu tribute from Rong and Di stopped; he marched west against the Quanrong, seized five of their kings, took four white deer and four white wolves, and resettled the Rong in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 夷王衰弱，荒服不朝，乃命虢公率六师伐太原之戎，至于俞泉，获马千匹。

translations.literal: King Yi weakened; the wild domains ceased court visits; he ordered the Duke of Guo to lead six armies against the Taiyuan Rong as far as Yuquan and capture a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi grew feeble the outer domains stayed away; he sent the Duke of Guo with six divisions against the Taiyuan Rong to Yuquan and brought back a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 厉王无道，戎狄寇掠，乃入犬丘，杀秦仲之族。

translations.literal: King Li was without the Way; Rong and Di raided and plundered, entered Quanqiu, and slew the clan of Zhong of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ruthless Li the Rong and Di swept in, reached Quanqiu, and wiped out Zhong of Qin's kin.

sentences.zh: 王命伐戎，不克。

translations.literal: The king ordered an attack on the Rong; it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Royal troops were ordered against the Rong but failed.

sentences.zh: 及宣王立四年，使秦仲伐戎，为戎所杀。

translations.literal: When King Xuan had been on the throne four years he sent Zhong of Qin against the Rong; Zhong was killed by the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuan's fourth year Zhong of Qin attacked the Rong and fell to them.

sentences.zh: 王乃召秦仲子庄公，与兵七千人伐戎，破之，由是少却。

translations.literal: The king then summoned Zhong's son Duke Zhuang, gave him seven thousand soldiers to attack the Rong, broke them, and thereafter they drew back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The king called up Zhuang, Zhong's son, armed him with seven thousand men, routed the Rong, and they slackened their pressure.

sentences.zh: 后二十七年，王遣兵伐太原戎，不克。

translations.literal: Twenty-seven years later the king sent troops against the Taiyuan Rong without success.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven years on another royal expedition against the Taiyuan Rong failed.

sentences.zh: 后五年，王伐条戎、奔戎，王师败绩。

translations.literal: Five years later the king attacked the Tiao Rong and Ben Rong; the royal army suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Five years after that he struck the Tiao and Ben Rong and his army was beaten.

sentences.zh: 后二年，晋人败北戎于汾隰，戎人灭姜侯之邑。

translations.literal: Two years later the people of Jin defeated the northern Rong at Fenxi; the Rong destroyed the town of the Jiang marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on Jin crushed the northern Rong at Fenxi while the Rong razed the Jiang lord's seat.

sentences.zh: 明年，王征申戎，破之。

translations.literal: The next year the king campaigned against the Shen Rong and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he attacked the Shen Rong and prevailed.

sentences.zh: 后十年，幽王命伯士伐六济之戎，军败，伯士死焉。

translations.literal: Ten years later King You ordered Boshi against the Liuji Rong; the army was defeated and Boshi died there.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later You sent Boshi against the Liuji Rong; the force was routed and Boshi fell.

sentences.zh: 其年，戎围犬丘，虏秦襄公之兄伯父。

translations.literal: That same year the Rong besieged Quanqiu and captured Bo Fu, elder brother of Duke Xiang of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: That year Rong invested Quanqiu and took Bo Fu, Xiang of Qin's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 时幽王昏虐，四夷交侵，遂废申后而立褒姒。

translations.literal: At that time You was benighted and cruel; the four barbarians attacked together; he then deposed the Shen queen and installed Baosi.
translations.idiomatic: You's reign brought invasion from every quarter; he cast aside Queen Shen and raised Baosi.

sentences.zh: 申侯怒，与戎寇周，杀幽王于郦山，周乃东迁洛邑，秦襄公攻戎救周。

translations.literal: Marquis Shen in anger joined the Rong in raiding Zhou, slew You at Lishan, Zhou then moved east to Luoyi, and Duke Xiang of Qin attacked Rong to rescue Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Marquis Shen allied with Rong against Zhou, killed You at Lishan, forced the court east to Luoyi, while Xiang of Qin struck Rong to aid the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 后二年，邢侯大破北戎。

translations.literal: Two years later Marquis Xing of Jin shattered the northern Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Two years afterward Xing of Jin broke the northern Rong.

sentences.zh: 及平王之末，周遂陵迟，戎逼诸夏，自陇山以东，及乎伊、洛，往往有戎。

translations.literal: By the end of King Ping's reign Zhou had declined; Rong pressed the Hua Xia lands; from east of Mount Long to the Yi and Luo rivers Rong were everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Ping's day Zhou slid downhill; Rong hemmed in the central states from east of Longshan to the Yi and Luo valleys.

sentences.zh: 于是渭首有狄、<豸原>、邽、冀之戎，泾北有义渠之戎，洛川有大荔之戎，渭南有骊戎，伊、洛间有杨拒、泉皋之戎，颍首以西有蛮氏之戎。

translations.literal: Then at the head of the Wei were the Di, Yuan, Gui, and Ji Rong; north of the Jing was the Yiqu Rong; on the Luo plain was the Dali Rong; south of the Wei was the Li Rong; between the Yi and Luo were the Yangju and Quangao Rong; west of the Ying headwaters was the Manshi Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At Wei's upper reaches stood the Di Rong, the Yuan Rong, the Gui Rong, and the Ji Rong; north of the Jing lay the Yiqu Rong; on the Luo plain stood the Dali Rong; south of the Wei lay the Li Rong; between the Yi and Luo lay the Yangju and Quangao Rong; west of the Ying headwaters lay the Manshi Rong.

sentences.zh: 当春秋时，间在中国，与诸夏盟会。

translations.literal: During the Spring and Autumn period they dwelled intermittently within China and joined the Hua Xia in covenants and meetings.
translations.idiomatic: In Spring and Autumn times they lodged inside the heartland at intervals and sat with the Zhou states in alliance.

sentences.zh: 鲁庄公伐秦，取邽、冀之戎。

translations.literal: Duke Zhuang of Lu attacked Qin and took the Gui and Ji Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's Duke Zhuang invaded Qin and seized the Gui and Ji Rong.

sentences.zh: 后十余岁，晋灭骊戎。

translations.literal: After more than ten years Jin extinguished the Li Rong.
translations.idiomatic: A decade later Jin destroyed the Li Rong.

sentences.zh: 是时，伊、洛戎强，东侵曹、鲁。

translations.literal: At that time the Yi and Luo Rong were strong and invaded east into Cao and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Yi–Luo Rong grew bold and pushed east against Cao and Lu.

sentences.zh: 后十九年，遂入王城。

translations.literal: Nineteen years later they entered the royal capital.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen years on they broke into the king's city.

sentences.zh: 于是秦、晋伐戎以救周。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qin and Jin attacked Rong to rescue Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Jin then struck Rong to relieve Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后二年，又寇京师，齐桓公征诸侯戍周。

translations.literal: Two years later they again raided the capital region; Duke Huan of Qi mobilized the feudal lords to garrison Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after that they harried the capital district until Huan of Qi called up the allies to guard Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后九年，陆浑戎自瓜州迁于伊川，允姓戎迁于渭汭，东及轘辕。

translations.literal: Nine years later the Luhun Rong moved from Guazhou to Yichuan; the Yun surname Rong moved to Weirui, reaching east to Huanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Nine years on Luhun Rong relocated from Guazhou to Yichuan and Yun-surname Rong to the Weirui, stretching east to Huanyuan.

sentences.zh: 在河南山北者号曰阴戎，阴戎之种遂以滋广。

translations.literal: Those north of Henan's mountains were called the Yin Rong; the Yin Rong strains thereby grew broad.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Henan range they were styled Yin Rong, and that stock spread wide.

sentences.zh: 晋文公欲修霸业，乃赂戎狄通道，以匡王室。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin wished to cultivate hegemony; he therefore bribed Rong and Di to open roads to restore the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Wen of Jin sought hegemonic sway and bought passage through Rong and Di to buttress the Zhou throne.

sentences.zh: 秦穆公得戎人由余，遂霸西戎，开地千里。

translations.literal: Duke Mu of Qin obtained You Yu of the Rong, then dominated the western Rong and opened a thousand li of territory.
translations.idiomatic: Mu of Qin won the defector You Yu, mastered the western Rong, and added a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 及晋悼公，又使魏绛和诸戎，复修霸业。

translations.literal: Down to Duke Dao of Jin he again sent Wei Jiang to reconcile the various Rong and renew hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dao of Jin, Wei Jiang again pacified the Rong camps and revived Jin's leadership.

sentences.zh: 是时，楚、晋强盛，威服诸戎，陆浑、伊、洛、阴戎事晋，而蛮氏从楚。

translations.literal: At that time Chu and Jin were mighty and overawed the Rong; Luhun, Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong served Jin while Manshi followed Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Chu and Jin towered above the Rong; Luhun, Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong backed Jin, Manshi Chu.

sentences.zh: 后陆浑叛晋，晋令荀吴灭之。

translations.literal: Later Luhun rebelled against Jin; Jin ordered Xun Wu to destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: When Luhun turned on Jin, Xun Wu wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 后四十四年，楚执蛮氏而尽囚其人。

translations.literal: Forty-four years later Chu seized Manshi and imprisoned all its people.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-four years on Chu seized Manshi and jailed its entire population.

sentences.zh: 是时义渠、大荔最强，筑城数十，皆自称王。

translations.literal: At that time Yiqu and Dali were strongest; they built several tens of cities and each styled himself king.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqu and Dali were then supreme, raising dozens of walled seats and each claiming kingship.

sentences.zh: 至周贞王八年，秦厉公分灭大荔，取其地。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of King Zhending of Zhou, Duke Li of Qin jointly extinguished Dali and took its land.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending's eighth year saw Li of Qin ally to crush Dali and annex its ground.

sentences.zh: 赵亦灭代戎，即北戎也。

translations.literal: Zhao also destroyed the Dai Rong; these were the northern Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao likewise erased the Dai Rong—that is, the northern Rong.

sentences.zh: 韩、魏复共稍并伊、洛、阴戎，灭之。

translations.literal: Han and Wei together gradually annexed the Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong and wiped them out.
translations.idiomatic: Han and Wei piecemeal swallowed the Yi, Luo, and Yin Rong.

sentences.zh: 其遗脱者皆逃走，西逾汧、陇。

translations.literal: Those who escaped fled west across the Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors bolted west over Qian and Long.

sentences.zh: 自是中国无戎寇，唯余义渠种焉。

translations.literal: From then on China had no Rong raids; only the Yiqu strain remained.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the heartland saw no Rong incursions—only Yiqu survived.

sentences.zh: 至贞王二十五年，秦伐义渠，虏其王。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Zhending Qin attacked Yiqu and captured its king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending's twenty-fifth year Qin struck Yiqu and took its king.

sentences.zh: 后十四年，义渠侵秦至渭阴。

translations.literal: Fourteen years later Yiqu invaded Qin as far as Weiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years on Yiqu pushed into Qin to Weiyin.

sentences.zh: 后百许年，义渠败秦师于洛。

translations.literal: About a hundred years later Yiqu defeated Qin's army at the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Roughly a century later Yiqu broke Qin's host on the Luo.

sentences.zh: 后四年，义渠国乱，秦惠王遣庶长操将兵定之，义渠遂臣于秦。

translations.literal: Four years later Yiqu's state fell into turmoil; King Hui of Qin sent the general Cao with troops to settle it, and Yiqu then submitted to Qin as subject.
translations.idiomatic: Four years after that Yiqu convulsed within; Hui of Qin dispatched Cao to pacify it, and Yiqu became Qin's vassal.

sentences.zh: 后八年，秦伐义渠，取郁郅。

translations.literal: Eight years later Qin attacked Yiqu and took Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Eight years on Qin seized Yuzhi from Yiqu.

sentences.zh: 后二年，义渠败秦师于李伯。

translations.literal: Two years later Yiqu defeated Qin's army at Libo.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Yiqu routed Qin at Libo.

sentences.zh: 明年，秦伐义渠，取徒泾二十五城。

translations.literal: The next year Qin attacked Yiqu and took twenty-five cities along Tujing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Qin took twenty-five Tujing towns from Yiqu.

sentences.zh: 及昭王立，义渠王朝秦，遂与昭王母宣太后通，生二子。

translations.literal: When King Zhao acceded, the king of Yiqu attended court at Qin; he then had illicit relations with King Zhao's mother Queen Dowager Xuan and fathered two sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's accession brought Yiqu's king to Qin's court; he became Queen Dowager Xuan's lover and sired two sons.

sentences.zh: 至王赧四十三年，宣太后诱杀义渠王于甘泉宫，因起兵灭之，始置陇西、北地、上郡焉。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of King Nan she lured the king of Yiqu to Ganquan Palace and murdered him, then raised troops to destroy Yiqu and first established Longxi, Beidi, and Shang commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In Nan's forty-third year Xuan murdered Yiqu's king at Ganquan, mustered an army to finish Yiqu, and first set up Longxi, Beidi, and Shang.

sentences.zh: 戎本无君长，夏后氏末及商周之际，或从侯伯征伐有功，天子爵之，以为籓服。

translations.literal: Originally Rong had no rulers; toward the end of the Xia and at the Shang-Zhou transition some followed marquises and earls on campaign with merit; the Son of Heaven ennobled them and kept them as outer domain.
translations.idiomatic: The Rong began without kings; late Xia into Shang-Zhou some fought under feudal lords and earned ranks from the Son of Heaven as outer dependents.

sentences.zh: 春秋时，陆浑、蛮氏戎称子。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times Luhun and Manshi Rong styled themselves viscounts.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and Autumn records show Luhun and Manshi Rong using the title “viscount.

sentences.zh: 战国世，大荔、义渠称王。

translations.literal: In the Warring States age Dali and Yiqu called themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Warring States saw Dali and Yiqu claim royal titles.

sentences.zh: 及其衰亡，余种皆反旧为酋豪云。

translations.literal: When they perished the surviving remnants all reverted to being chieftains as of old.
translations.idiomatic: After their fall the remnants returned to chieftain rule as before.

sentences.zh: 羌无弋爰剑者，秦厉公时为秦所拘执，以为奴隶。

translations.literal: There was Yuanjian of the Qiang of the Wuyi line; in the time of Duke Li of Qin he was seized by Qin and made a slave.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chieftain Yuanjian, who bore the epithet Wuyi, was captured under Duke Li of Qin and reduced to slavery.

sentences.zh: 不知爰剑何戎之别也。

translations.literal: It is not known which Rong branch Yuanjian belonged to.
translations.idiomatic: His exact Rong affiliation is unknown.

sentences.zh: 后得亡归，而秦人追之急，藏于岩穴中得免。

translations.literal: Later he escaped and returned; Qin pursued him urgently; he hid in a cliff cave and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He fled homeward under hot pursuit and hid in a rock cave until the chase gave up.

sentences.zh: 羌人云爰剑初藏穴中，秦人焚之，有景象如虎，为其蔽火，得以不死。

translations.literal: The Qiang relate that when Yuanjian first hid in the cave Qin men burned it; a tiger-like apparition shielded him from the fire so he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang tradition says fire set by Qin could not kill him because a tiger-shaped spirit beat the flames away.

sentences.zh: 既出，又与劓女遇于野，遂成夫妇。

translations.literal: After he emerged he met in the wild a woman whose nose had been cut off; they became husband and wife.
translations.idiomatic: Once out he paired with a noseless woman met in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 女耻其状，被发覆面，羌人因以为俗，遂俱亡入三河间。

translations.literal: The woman was ashamed of her appearance; she let her hair hang loose to cover her face; the Qiang took this as custom; together they fled into the region of the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: She veiled her face with loose hair from shame; the Qiang adopted the habit and both fled into the Three Rivers country.

sentences.zh: 诸羌见爰剑被焚不死，怪其神，共畏事之，推以为豪，河湟间少五谷，多禽兽，以射猎为事，爰剑教之田畜，遂见敬信，庐落种人依之者日益众。

translations.literal: The various Qiang saw Yuanjian emerge unscathed from the fire, marveled at his spirit, all feared and served him, and pushed him to be chief; between the Huang and Huang loop grain was scarce and game plentiful; they lived by hunting; Yuanjian taught them farming and herding; he won reverence and trust; camps and tribes dependent on him grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him survive the blaze they revered him as spirit-made, made him chief, and learned tillage and stock-rearing in the Huang valleys where hunt had once ruled; his following swelled.

sentences.zh: 羌人谓奴为无弋，以爰剑尝为奴隶，故因名之。

translations.literal: The Qiang call a slave Wu Yi; because Yuanjian had been a slave they therefore named him so.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yi meant “slave” in Qiang speech; Yuanjian kept the epithet because Qin had bound him.

sentences.zh: 其后世世为豪。

translations.literal: Afterward generation upon generation were chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: His line stayed paramount for generations.

sentences.zh: 至爰剑曾孙忍时，秦献公初立，欲复穆公之迹，兵临渭首，灭狄獂戎。

translations.literal: Down to Yuanjian's great-grandson Ren, Duke Xian of Qin first took the throne, wished to resume Duke Mu's achievements, brought troops to the head of the Wei, and extinguished the Di Yuan Rong.
translations.idiomatic: At Ren, Xian of Qin sought to replay Mu's glory, marched to Wei's head, and wiped out the Di Yuan Rong.

sentences.zh: 忍季父卯畏秦之威，将其种人附落而南，出赐支河曲西数千里，与众羌绝远，不复交通。

translations.literal: Ren's uncle Mao feared Qin's might, led his tribesmen's dependent camps south, went out several thousand li west of the Zhizhi bend, and broke contact with the other Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle Mao, cowed by Qin, led dependents south beyond the Zhizhi bend for thousands of li, cutting ties with fellow Qiang.

sentences.zh: 其后子孙分别，各自为种，任随所之。

translations.literal: Later descendants split apart and each became its own strain, going wherever they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Later kin fragmented into separate tribes wherever they wandered.

sentences.zh: 或为牦牛种，越巂羌是也；

translations.literal: Some became the yak strain—the Yuexi Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: One branch became the yak people—the Yuexi Qiang.

sentences.zh: 或为白马种，广汉羌是也；

translations.literal: Some became the white-horse strain—the Guanghan Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Another became the white-horse people—the Guanghan Qiang.

sentences.zh: 或为参狼种，武都羌是也。

translations.literal: Some became the wolf strain—the Wudu Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: A third became the wolf people—the Wudu Qiang.

sentences.zh: 忍及弟舞独留湟中，并多娶妻妇。

translations.literal: Ren and his younger brother Wu alone remained in the Huang loop and both took many wives.
translations.idiomatic: Ren and Wu stayed in the Huang heartland and married widely.

sentences.zh: 忍生九子为九种，舞生十七子为十七种，羌之兴盛，从此起矣。

translations.literal: Ren fathered nine sons who became nine strains; Wu fathered seventeen sons who became seventeen strains; the rise and flowering of the Qiang began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From Ren came nine branches and from Wu seventeen; the great expansion of the Qiang people dates to that multiplication.

sentences.zh: 及忍子研立，时秦孝公雄强，威服羌戎。

translations.literal: When Ren's son Yan assumed leadership, Duke Xiao of Qin was mighty and strong and overawed the Qiang and Rong into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yan's chieftaincy Duke Xiao of Qin towered in power and bent every Qiang and Rong camp to his will.

sentences.zh: 孝公使太子驷率戎狄九十二国朝周显王。

translations.literal: Duke Xiao sent Crown Prince Si to lead ninety-two states of Rong and Di to present themselves at the court of King Xian of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao dispatched the heir Si at the head of ninety-two Rong and Di polities to do homage to Zhou's King Xian.

sentences.zh: 研至豪健，故羌中号其后为研种。

translations.literal: Yan was supremely robust and brave; therefore among the Qiang his posterity were called the Yan strain.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's singular vigor won his line the tribal name Yan.

sentences.zh: 及秦始皇时，务并六国，以诸侯为事，兵不西行，故种人得以繁息。

translations.literal: Down to Qin Shi Huang the priority was annexing the six states and dealing with the feudal lords; troops did not march westward; therefore the tribes could breed and multiply.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor fixed on swallowing the six kingdoms and never sent armies west, so the highland peoples flourished unchecked.

sentences.zh: 秦既兼天下，使蒙恬将兵略地，西逐诸戎，北却众狄，筑长城以界之，众羌不服南度。

translations.literal: Once Qin had united the realm it sent Meng Tian with troops to seize ground, drove the various Rong westward, pushed the mass of Di back in the north, and built the Long Wall to mark the boundary; the mass of Qiang would not submit and crossed southward.
translations.idiomatic: After unification Meng Tian cleared the west and north and walled them off; the Qiang who refused that partition slipped southward.

sentences.zh: 至于汉兴，匈奴冒顿兵强，破东胡，走月氏，威震百蛮，臣服诸羌。

translations.literal: When Han arose, the Xiongnu ruler Modun's army was strong; he shattered the Eastern Hu, drove off the Yuezhi, his might shook the hundred barbarians, and the various Qiang submitted as vassals.
translations.idiomatic: Han's rise coincided with Modun's zenith: he broke the Eastern Hu, expelled the Yuezhi, terrified every frontier people, and brought the Qiang tribes to allegiance.

sentences.zh: 景帝时，研种留何率种人求守陇西塞，于是徙留何等于狄道、安故，至临洮、氐道、羌道县。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Jing, Liu He of the Yan strain led his tribesmen to request duty guarding the Longxi frontier; thereupon Liu He and the rest were relocated to Didao and Angu, reaching as far as the counties Lintao, Didao, and Qiangdao.
translations.idiomatic: Jing accepted Liu He's offer to hold the Longxi line and resettled his band through Didao, Angu, Lintao, and the Di- and Qiang-named counties.

sentences.zh: 及武帝征伐四夷，开地广境，北却匈奴，西逐诸羌，乃度河、湟，筑令居塞、初开河西，列置四郡，通道玉门，隔绝羌胡，使南北不得交关。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against the four barbarians, opened territory and widened the borders, drove back the Xiongnu in the north and chased the various Qiang westward, he then crossed the Huang and Huang rivers, built Lingju Barrier, first opened the Hexi corridor, established four commanderies in a row, opened the road through Jade Gate, cut off Qiang from the Hu, and prevented north and south from linking.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Di's western wars pushed the Xiongnu back, bridged the Huang loop, threw up Lingju, colonized Hexi with four commanderies, opened Jade Gate, and severed Qiang from the steppe so neither flank could unite.

sentences.zh: 于是障塞亭燧出长城外数千里。

translations.literal: Thereupon barrier ramparts, fortresses, and beacon lines ran several thousand li beyond the Long Wall.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier walls, posts, and smoke towers soon stretched thousands of li past the old Qin barrier.

sentences.zh: 时先零羌与封养牢姐种解仇结盟，与匈奴通，合兵十余万，共攻令居、安故，遂围枹罕。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianling Qiang and the Fengyang Laojie strain broke old grudges and swore alliance, communicated with the Xiongnu, united armies over a hundred thousand strong, and jointly attacked Lingju and Angu, then besieged Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianling joined Laojie, allied with the Xiongnu, and swept over a hundred thousand fighters against Lingju, Angu, and Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 汉遣将军李息、郎中令徐自为将兵十万人击平之。

translations.literal: Han dispatched General Li Xi and Palace Superintendent Xu Ziwei with a hundred thousand troops to strike and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Li Xi and Xu Ziwei at the head of one hundred thousand men to crush the rising.

sentences.zh: 始置护羌校尉，持节统领焉。

translations.literal: It first established the Colonel Protector of the Qiang, bearing credentials to command them.
translations.idiomatic: For the first time a Colonel Protector of the Qiang was appointed with imperial staff to oversee the tribes.

sentences.zh: 羌乃去湟中，依西海、盐池左右。

translations.literal: The Qiang then left the Zhong loop and lodged by the Western Sea and the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew from Zhong to range along the Western Sea and the brine lakes.

sentences.zh: 汉遂因山为寒，河西地空，稍徙人以实之。

translations.literal: Han therefore relied on mountains for barriers; Hexi lay empty and people were gradually moved in to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: The dynasty ran mountain barriers along the new line while settlers filled an emptied Hexi.

sentences.zh: 至宣帝时，遣光禄大夫义渠安国觇行诸羌，其先零种豪言：“愿得度湟水，逐人所不田处以为畜牧。

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Xuan it sent Palace Counsellor Yiqu Anguo to tour and observe the various Qiang; a Xianling chieftain boasted: "We wish to cross the Huang River and pasture where others do not till."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Yiqu Anguo to inspect the tribes; a Xianling headman asked leave to ford the Huang and graze untilled ground.

sentences.zh: ”安国以事奏闻，后将军赵充国以为不可听。

translations.literal: " Anguo reported the matter; Rear General Zhao Chongguo deemed it must not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo memorialized; Zhao Chongguo urged refusal.

sentences.zh: 后因缘前言，遂度湟水，郡县不能禁。

translations.literal: Later on the strength of that earlier remark they crossed the Huang; commanderies and counties could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: They cited the old pledge, crossed anyway, and local officials proved helpless.

sentences.zh: 至元康三年，先零乃与诸羌大共盟誓，将欲寇边。

translations.literal: By the third year of Yuankang the Xianling had sworn a great oath with the various Qiang and intended to raid the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuankang's third year Xianling bound every major tribe by oath for a frontier strike.

sentences.zh: 帝闻，复使安国将兵观之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he again sent Anguo with troops to observe them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne dispatched Anguo again with an army to reconnoitre.

sentences.zh: 安国至，召先零豪四十余人斩之，因放兵击其种，斩首千余级。

translations.literal: When Anguo arrived he summoned more than forty Xianling chieftains and executed them, then unleashed troops against their strain, taking over a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Anguo decapitated forty-odd chiefs and slaughtered their followers for a thousand-level body count.

sentences.zh: 于是诸羌怨怒，遂寇金城。

translations.literal: Thereupon the various Qiang were resentful and angry and raided Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribe turned hostile and fell on Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 乃遣赵充国与诸将将兵六万人击破平之。

translations.literal: It then dispatched Zhao Chongguo and various generals with sixty thousand troops to defeat and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongguo and allied commanders marched sixty thousand men to break them.

sentences.zh: 至研十三世孙烧当立。

translations.literal: Down to the thirteenth-generation descendant of Yan, Shaodang, who assumed leadership.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen generations from Yan, Shaodang took the chieftaincy.

sentences.zh: 元帝时，彡姐等七种羌寇陇西，遣右将军冯奉世击破降之。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yuan the Shan Jie and seven other Qiang strains raided Longxi; it sent Right General Feng Fengshi to defeat and reduce them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's reign saw seven Qiang groups, Shan Jie among them, strike Longxi until Feng Fengshi crushed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 从爰剑种五世至研，研最豪健，自后以研为种号。

translations.literal: From Yuanjian's strain five generations down to Yan; Yan was the most robust and brave; thereafter they took Yan as the strain name.
translations.idiomatic: Five generations out from Yuanjian stood Yan, the mightiest of his line, whose name became the tribal label.

sentences.zh: 十三世至烧当，复豪健，其子孙更以烧当为种号。

translations.literal: Thirteen generations on to Shaodang, again robust and brave; his descendants in turn took Shaodang as the strain name.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen generations later Shaodang matched that fame; his heirs bore his name as their branch.

sentences.zh: 自彡姐羌降之后数十年，四夷宾服，边塞无事。

translations.literal: After the Shan Jie Qiang submitted, several decades passed with the four barbarians attending court and the frontier quiet.
translations.idiomatic: For decades after Shan Jie's surrender the outer peoples paid homage and the passes stayed still.

sentences.zh: 至王莽辅政，欲燿威德，以怀远为名，乃令译讽旨诸羌，使共献西海之地，初开以为郡，筑五县，边海亭燧相望焉。

translations.literal: When Wang Mang assisted in government he wished to display might and virtue; under the name of cherishing the distant he ordered interpreters to convey his intent to the various Qiang and made them jointly present the Western Sea lands; he first opened them as a commandery, built five counties, and coastal frontier beacons stood in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Mang courted glory by inducing the Qiang to "offer" the Western Sea, annexed it as a commandery with five counties, and strung watchfires along the shore.

sentences.zh: 滇良者，烧当之玄孙也。

translations.literal: Dianliang was the great-great-grandson of Shaodang.
translations.idiomatic: Dianliang descended from Shaodang in the fourth generation.

sentences.zh: 时王莽末，四夷内侵，及莽败，众羌遂还据西海为寇。

translations.literal: At the end of Wang Mang's time the four barbarians pressed inward; when Mang fell the mass of Qiang returned to occupy the Western Sea as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Late Mang saw invasion on every side; after his fall the Qiang reclaimed the Western Sea as a base.

sentences.zh: 更始、赤眉之际，羌遂放纵，寇金城、陇西。

translations.literal: Amid Gengshi and the Red Eyebrows the Qiang ran wild, raiding Jincheng and Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Through Gengshi and the Red Eyebrows they plundered Jincheng and Longxi.

sentences.zh: 隗嚣虽拥兵而不能讨之，乃就慰纳，因发其众与汉相拒。

translations.literal: Although Wei Ao held troops he could not chastise them; he therefore went to comfort and absorb them and mobilized their masses to resist Han.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ao could not suppress them; he coaxed them into his war against Han.

sentences.zh: 建武九年，隗嚣死，司徒掾班彪上言：“今凉州部皆有降羌，羌胡被发左衽，而与汉人杂处，习俗既异，言语不通。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jianwu, when Wei Ao died, Steward-in-chief clerk Ban Biao submitted: "Now every circuit of Liangzhou harbors surrendered Qiang; Qiang and Hu wear their hair loose and fasten lapels left, yet dwell mixed among Han; customs differ and speech does not meet."
translations.idiomatic: After Ao died in Jianwu 9, Ban Biao warned that surrendered Qiang and Hu in Liangzhou, clothed and tongued unlike Han neighbors, were powder kegs.

sentences.zh: 数为小吏黠人所见侵夺，穷恚无聊，故致反叛。

translations.literal: Repeatedly petty clerks and crafty men saw them violated and plundered; destitute and furious with nothing left, they therefore turned rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Petty officials preyed on them until desperation drove them to revolt.

sentences.zh: 夫蛮夷寇乱，皆为此也。

translations.literal: As for barbarian raids and turmoil, all arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier risings, he argued, all stemmed from such abuse.

sentences.zh: 旧制：益州部署蛮夷骑都尉，幽州部署领乌桓校尉，凉州部署护羌校尉，皆持节领护，理其怨结，岁时循行，问所疾苦。

translations.literal: Old regulation: Yizhou posted a Cavalry Commandant for barbarians, Youzhou an Colonel Commanding the Wuhuan, Liangzhou a Colonel Protector of the Qiang, all bearing credentials to lead and protect, settle grievances, and annually tour to ask what pained them.
translations.idiomatic: The old system gave each region a credentialed officer to hear complaints and make yearly rounds.

sentences.zh: 又数遣使驿通动静，使塞外羌夷为吏耳目，州郡因此可得儆备。

translations.literal: Moreover envoys were repeatedly sent by post relay to learn movements, making Qiang and Yi beyond the passes the officials' eyes and ears so commanderies and prefectures could stay on guard.
translations.idiomatic: Courier posts and frontier informants had once kept the court warned.

sentences.zh: 今宜复如旧，以明威防。

translations.literal: Now it is fitting to restore this as of old to clarify awe and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Ban urged restoring those posts to show authority and foresight.

sentences.zh: ”光武从之，即以牛邯为护羌校尉，持节如旧。

translations.literal: " Guangwu assented and immediately appointed Niu Han Colonel Protector of the Qiang with credentials as before.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu agreed and named Niu Han colonel with the old powers.

sentences.zh: 及邯卒而职省。

translations.literal: When Han died the office was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At Han's death the post lapsed.

sentences.zh: 十年，先零豪与诸种相结，复寇金城、陇西，遣中郎将来歙等击之，大破。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Xianling chieftains allied with various strains again raided Jincheng and Longxi; it sent Palace Gentlemen Lai Xi and others against them and shattered them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xianling chiefs allied with other bands and struck Jincheng and Longxi again until Lai Xi routed them.

sentences.zh: 事已具《歙传》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully given in the "Biography of Xi".
translations.idiomatic: The full account stands in the memoir on Xi.

sentences.zh: 十一年夏，先零种复寇临洮，陇西太守马援破降之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the eleventh year the Xianling strain again raided Lintao; Longxi Governor Ma Yuan defeated and reduced them.
translations.idiomatic: Summer of year 11 saw Ma Yuan smash a Lintao raid.

sentences.zh: 后悉归服，徙置天水、陇西、扶风三郡。

translations.literal: Later all submitted and were moved into Tianshui, Longxi, and Fufeng commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: They eventually surrendered and were settled across Tianshui, Longxi, and Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 明年，武都参狼羌反，援又破降之。

translations.literal: The next year the Canlang Qiang of Wudu rebelled; Yuan again defeated and reduced them.
translations.idiomatic: The Canlang of Wudu rose the following year and Yuan pacified them too.

sentences.zh: 事已具《援传》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully given in the "Biography of Yuan".
translations.idiomatic: The campaign is recorded in Yuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 自烧当至滇良，世居河北大允谷，种小人贫。

translations.literal: From Shaodang down to Dianliang they generation after generation dwelt north of the river in Great Allow Valley; the strain was small and the people poor.
translations.idiomatic: Shaodang's line lived north of the river in Dayun Valley, few and poor.

sentences.zh: 而先零、卑湳并皆强富，数侵犯之。

translations.literal: But Xianling and Beinan were both strong and rich and repeatedly violated them.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy Xianling and Beinan bullied them often.

sentences.zh: 滇良父子积见陵易，愤怒，而素有恩信于种中，于是集会附落及诸杂种，乃从大榆入，掩击先零、卑湳，大破之，杀三千人，掠取财畜，夺居其地大榆中，由是始强。

translations.literal: Dianliang and his son had long suffered bullying and humiliation; angry, yet they had long held good faith among the tribes; thereupon they assembled dependent camps and miscellaneous strains, entered by Great Elm, fell upon Xianling and Beinan, shattered them, killed three thousand, plundered wealth and livestock, seized and occupied their territory in Great Elm, and from this grew strong.
translations.idiomatic: Dianliang rallied dependents, struck through Dayu, crushed Xianling and Beinan for three thousand dead, looted their herds, and took Dayu ground—his power dated from that coup.

sentences.zh: 滇良子滇吾立。

translations.literal: Dianliang's son Dianwu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Dianwu followed his father.

sentences.zh: 中元元年，武都参狼羌反，杀略吏人，太守与战不胜，陇西太守刘盱遣从事辛都、监军掾李苞，将五千人赴武都，与羌战，斩其酋豪，首虏千余人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongyuan the Canlang Qiang of Wudu rebelled, killing and robbing officials and people; the governor fought them without victory; Longxi Governor Liu Xu sent aide Xin Du and supervising clerk Li Bao with five thousand men to Wudu, fought the Qiang, beheaded their chieftains, and took over a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyuan 1 saw Wudu's Canlang kill and loot until Liu Xu reinforced the governor with five thousand men and a thousand-level victory.

sentences.zh: 时，武都兵亦更破之，斩首千余级，余悉降。

translations.literal: At that time Wudu troops also again defeated them, taking over a thousand heads; the remainder all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Local forces added another thousand kills; the rest yielded.

sentences.zh: 时滇吾附落转盛，常雄诸羌，每欲侵边者，滇吾转教以方略，为其渠帅。

translations.literal: At that time Dianwu's dependent camp grew powerful; he constantly dominated the various Qiang; whenever any wished to raid the border Dianwu taught them plans and served as their chief.
translations.idiomatic: Dianwu's following swelled until he lorded over other Qiang, coaching every raid and acting as supreme chief.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，烧当羌滇吾与弟滇岸率步骑五千寇陇西塞，刘盱遣兵于枹罕击之，不能克，又战于允街，为羌所败，杀五百余人。

translations.literal: In the second year autumn the Shaodang Qiang Dianwu and his younger brother Dian'an led five thousand foot and horse to raid the Longxi frontier; Liu Xu sent troops against them at Fuhan without success; they fought again at Yunjie and were defeated by the Qiang, losing over five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn of year 2: Dianwu and Dian'an hit Longxi with five thousand riders; Liu Xu lost at Fuhan and Yunjie, sacrificing five hundred.

sentences.zh: 于是守塞诸羌皆复相率为寇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qiang guarding the frontier all again joined ranks as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Qiang everywhere joined the storm.

sentences.zh: 遣谒者张鸿领诸郡兵击之，战于允吾、唐谷，军败，鸿及陇西长史田飒皆没。

translations.literal: It sent Herald Zhang Hong leading commandery troops against them; they fought at Yunwu and Tang valley; the army was defeated; Hong and Longxi chief clerk Tian Sa both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hong died with Tian Sa when their army broke at Yunwu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 又天水兵为牢姐种所败于白石，死者千余人。

translations.literal: Moreover Tianshui troops were defeated by the Laojie strain at Baishi with over a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshui lost another thousand to Laojie at Baishi.

sentences.zh: 时，烧何豪有妇人比铜钳者，年百余岁，多智算，为种人所信向，皆从取计策。

translations.literal: At that time among the Shaohe chieftains was a woman called Bitongqian, over a hundred years old, full of schemes; the tribes trusted and revered her and all took counsel from her.
translations.idiomatic: Among Shaohe elders lived Bitongqian, a centenarian tactician whom every band obeyed.

sentences.zh: 时为卢水胡所击，比铜钳乃将其众来依郡县。

translations.literal: At that time she was struck by the Lushui Hu; Bitongqian then led her masses to rely on commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Lushui Hu drove her to seek shelter under Han magistrates.

sentences.zh: 种人颇有犯法者，临羌长收系比铜钳，而诛杀其种六七百人。

translations.literal: Among the tribesmen quite a few broke the law; the chief of Linqiang seized and imprisoned Bitongqian and executed six or seven hundred of her strain.
translations.idiomatic: Linqiang's magistrate jailed her and slaughtered six or seven hundred of her kin.

sentences.zh: 显宗怜之，乃下诏曰：“昔桓公伐戎而无仁惠。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming pitied them and issued an edict: "Of old Duke Huan attacked the Rong without kindness or bounty.
translations.idiomatic: Ming issued pity: "Huan of Qi struck Rong without mercy.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》贬曰：‘齐人’。

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn censures him as 'men of Qi'."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Spring and Autumn dismisses them merely as 'Qi men.'"

sentences.zh: 今国家无德，恩不及远，羸弱何辜，而当并命！

translations.literal: Now the state lacks virtue; grace does not reach the distant; what crime have the weak committed that they should perish together!"
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty lacks virtue if the helpless must die for it!"

sentences.zh: 夫长平之暴，非帝者之功，咎由太守长吏妄加残戮。

translations.literal: As for the cruelty at Changping, it is no achievement fit for an emperor; the blame lies with governors and senior clerks who wantonly added slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Changping-style slaughter wins no true emperor; blame sits with cruel prefects.

sentences.zh: 比铜钳尚生者，所在致医药养视，令招其种人，若欲归故地者，厚遣送之。

translations.literal: Any Bitongqian still living shall wherever they are receive medicine and care; order her tribes summoned; if they wish to return to former lands send them generously on their way.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors get doctors and escort home whomsoever wishes to leave.

sentences.zh: 其小种若束手自诣，欲效功者，皆除其罪。

translations.literal: Lesser strains who bind their own hands and come in wishing to merit service shall all be cleared of guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Petty bands who surrender willingly may earn pardon.

sentences.zh: 若有逆谋，为吏所捕，而狱状未断，悉以赐有功者。

translations.literal: If there are those plotting rebellion whom clerks seize while suits remain undecided, award them all to the meritorious.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners awaiting verdict on rebellion charges may be granted as prizes to the worthy.
Here the edict's quotation closes.

sentences.zh: 永平元年，复遣中郎将窦固、捕虏将军马武等击滇吾于西邯，大破之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongping it again sent Palace General Dou Gu and Capturing-Barbarians General Ma Wu and others to strike Dianwu at Xihan and shattered him.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping 1: Dou Gu and Ma Wu ruined Dianwu at Xihan.

sentences.zh: 事已具武等传。

translations.literal: The affair is fully given in the biographies of Wu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and his colleagues have full memoirs.

sentences.zh: 滇吾远引去，余悉散降，徙七千口置三辅。

translations.literal: Dianwu withdrew far away; the remainder scattered and surrendered; seven thousand persons were moved into the Three Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Dianwu fled; captives filled seven thousand mouths resettled near the capital.

sentences.zh: 以谒者窦林领护羌校尉，居狄道。

translations.literal: Herald Dou Lin was appointed acting Colonel Protector of the Qiang and dwelt at Didao.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Lin took the colonelcy and headquartered at Didao.

sentences.zh: 林为诸羌所信，而滇岸遂诣林降。

translations.literal: Lin was trusted by the various Qiang and Dian'an therefore went to Lin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes trusted Lin; Dian'an came in through him.

sentences.zh: 林为下吏所欺，谬奏上滇岸以为大豪，承制封为归义侯，加号汉大都尉。

translations.literal: Lin was deceived by inferior clerks and falsely memorialized Dian'an as the great chieftain; receiving imperial orders he enfeoffed him as Marquis Who Returns to Righteousness with the added title Han Grand Commandant of the Metropolis.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates duped Lin into naming Dian'an paramount chief and minting him a bogus marquis and metropolitan commandant.

sentences.zh: 明年，滇吾复降，林复奏其第一豪，与俱诣阙献见。

translations.literal: The next year Dianwu again surrendered; Lin again memorialized him as first chieftain and accompanied him to the palace for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Dianwu yielded too; Lin hailed another "first chief" and marched both to court.

sentences.zh: 帝怪一种两豪，疑其非实，以事诘林。

translations.literal: The emperor wondered how one strain had two paramount chiefs and doubted the truth; he questioned Lin about the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The throne smelled fraud when two "supreme" leaders appeared.

sentences.zh: 林辞窘，乃伪对曰；

translations.literal: Lin's replies grew desperate; he falsely answered:
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Lin lied:

sentences.zh: “滇岸即滇吾，陇西语不正耳。

translations.literal: Open quotation mark preceding Lin's reply: Dian'an is identical with Dianwu; Longxi speech is simply imprecise.
translations.idiomatic: Lin claimed Dian'an and Dianwu were one man and blamed sloppy Longxi pronunciation.

sentences.zh: ”帝穷验知之，怒而免林官。

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark ending Lin's lie; the emperor exhaustively investigated and learned the truth; angry, he dismissed Lin from office.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation exposed the sham and cost Lin his post.

sentences.zh: 会凉州刺史又奏林臧罪，遂下狱死。

translations.literal: When moreover the Liangzhou inspector memorialized Lin's corruption crimes, he was cast into prison and died.
translations.idiomatic: An impeachment for graft sent him to die in jail.

sentences.zh: 谒者郭襄代领校尉事，到陇西，闻凉州羌盛，还诣阙，抵罪，于是复省校尉官。

translations.literal: Herald Guo Xiang succeeded to acting colonel affairs; reaching Longxi he heard Liangzhou Qiang were strong, returned to the palace to answer for crime; therefore the colonel office was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xiang fled back on news of Qiang strength and the colonelcy vanished again.

sentences.zh: 滇吾子东吾立，以父降汉，乃入居塞内，谨愿自守。

translations.literal: Dianwu's son Dongwu succeeded; because his father had surrendered to Han he entered to dwell inside the frontier and was cautious and wished only to keep the peace.
translations.idiomatic: Dongwu moved inside the wall after his father's submission and kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 而诸弟迷吾等数为寇盗。

translations.literal: But his younger brothers such as Miwu repeatedly acted as raiders and bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brothers like Miwu still harried the frontier.

sentences.zh: 肃宗建初元年，安夷县吏略妻卑湳种羌妇，吏为其夫所杀，安夷长宗延追之出塞，种人恐见诛，遂共杀延，而与勒姐及吾良二种相结为寇。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Zhang's Jianchu an Anyi clerk seized as wife a woman of the Beinan strain Qiang; the clerk was killed by her husband; Anyi chief Zong Yan pursued him beyond the pass; the tribes feared execution; they jointly killed Yan and allied with the Lejie and Wuliang strains as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Jianchu 1 opened with an Anyi clerk stealing a Beinan Qiang wife; her husband killed him; Zong Yan chased beyond the wall; dreading punishment the tribes slew Yan and joined Lejie and Wuliang.

sentences.zh: 陇西太守孙纯遣从事李睦及金城兵会和罗谷，与卑湳等战，斩首虏数百人。

translations.literal: Longxi Governor Sun Chun sent aide Li Mu and Jincheng troops to gather at Heluo valley and fought Beinan and others, taking several hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Chun's aide Li Mu joined Jincheng men at Heluo for a few hundred kills.

sentences.zh: 复拜故度辽将军吴棠领护羌校尉，居安夷。

translations.literal: It again appointed former General Who Crossed the Liao Wu Tang as Colonel Protector of the Qiang, dwelling at Anyi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Tang resumed the colonelcy based at Anyi.

sentences.zh: 二年夏，迷吾遂与诸众聚兵，欲叛出塞。

translations.literal: In the second year summer Miwu then gathered hosts with the masses intending to rebel and exit the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Summer of year 2: Miwu massed for a breakout.

sentences.zh: 金城太守郝崇追之，战于荔谷，崇兵大败，崇轻骑得脱，死者二千余人。

translations.literal: Jincheng Governor Hao Chong pursued them; they fought at Ligu; Chong's army was badly defeated; Chong escaped with light horse; over two thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Chong lost two thousand men escaping Ligu.

sentences.zh: 于是诸种及属国卢水胡悉与相应，吴棠不能制，坐征免。

translations.literal: Thereupon various strains together with dependent-state Lushui Hu all responded; Wu Tang could not control them and was summoned and dismissed for fault.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribe plus Lushui Hu answered Miwu; Tang fell from office.

sentences.zh: 武威太守傅育代为校尉，移居临羌。

translations.literal: Wuwei Governor Fu Yu succeeded as colonel and moved headquarters to Linqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yu of Wuwei replaced him at Linqiang.

sentences.zh: 迷吾又与封养种豪布桥等五万余人共寇陇西、汉阳，于是遣行车骑将军马防，长外校尉耿恭副，讨破之。

translations.literal: Miwu further joined Fengyang chieftains Bu Qiao and others, over fifty thousand strong, jointly raiding Longxi and Hanyang; thereupon it dispatched Acting Chariots-and-Cavalry General Ma Fang with Outer Colonel Geng Gong as deputy to strike and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Miwu and Bu Qiao led fifty thousand against Longxi and Hanyang until Ma Fang and Geng Gong broke them.

sentences.zh: 于是临洮、索西、迷吾等悉降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lintao, Suoxi, Miwu and others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Lintao, Suoxi, and Miwu soon capitulated.

sentences.zh: 防乃筑索西城，徙陇西南部都尉戍之，悉复诸亭候。

translations.literal: Fang then built Suoxi city, moved the southern division chief of Longxi to garrison it, and restored every pavilion and watch.
translations.idiomatic: Fang walled Suoxi, stationed Longxi's southern chief there, and rebuilt the watch chain.

sentences.zh: 至元和三年，迷吾复与弟号吾诸杂种反叛。

translations.literal: Down to the third year of Yuanhe Miwu again rebelled with his younger brother Haowu and miscellaneous strains.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhe 3 reignited Miwu, Haowu, and allies.

sentences.zh: 秋，号吾先轻入寇陇西界，郡督烽掾李章追之，生得号吾。

translations.literal: In autumn Haowu first lightly entered to raid Longxi territory; commandery signal-beacon clerk Li Zhang pursued him and captured Haowu alive.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Haowu probed Longxi until Li Zhang ran him down alive.

sentences.zh: 将诣郡，号吾曰：“独杀我，无损于羌。

translations.literal: About to be brought to the commandery Haowu said:
translations.idiomatic: Before the yamen Haowu pleaded:

sentences.zh: 诚得生归，必悉罢兵，不复犯塞。

translations.literal: "If I alone am killed it does no harm to the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: "Kill only me and the Qiang lose nothing.

sentences.zh: ”陇西太守张纡权宜放遣，羌即为解散，各归故地。

translations.literal: "If truly allowed to return alive I shall surely dismiss all troops and never again violate the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Let me live and I will disband every spear and never raid again.

sentences.zh: 迷吾退居河北归义城。

translations.literal: Miwu withdrew to dwell north of the river at Guiyi city.
translations.idiomatic: Miwu fell back north of the river to Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 傅育不欲失信伐之，乃募人斗诸羌胡，羌胡不肯，遂复叛出塞，更依迷吾。

translations.literal: Yu did not wish to break faith by attacking them; he therefore recruited men to fight the various Qiang and Hu; the Qiang and Hu refused; they therefore rebelled again and exited the pass, once more attaching themselves to Miwu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yu shrank from striking without cause and tried to pit allies against the tribes; when Qiang and Hu balked they bolted beyond the wall back to Miwu.

sentences.zh: 章和元年，育上请发陇西、张掖、酒泉各五千人，诸郡太守将之，育自领汉阳、金城五千人，合二万兵，与诸郡克期击之，令陇西兵据河南，张掖、酒泉兵遮其西。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhanghe Yu memorialized requesting that Longxi, Zhangye, and Jiuquan each dispatch five thousand men under their governors while he personally commanded five thousand from Hanyang and Jincheng, combining twenty thousand troops to strike on a fixed date with Longxi holding south of the river and Zhangye and Jiuquan blocking the west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanghe 1: Yu asked for five thousand each from Longxi, Zhangye, and Jiuquan plus five thousand of his own from Hanyang and Jincheng—twenty thousand in all—with a pincer south of the river and along the west.

sentences.zh: 并未及会，育军独进。

translations.literal: The allied hosts had not yet met when Yu's army advanced alone.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rendezvous Yu marched ahead with only his own column.

sentences.zh: 迷吾闻之，徙庐落去，育选精骑三千穷追之，夜至建威南三兜谷，去虏数里，须旦击之，不设备。

translations.literal: When Miwu heard this he moved his camps away; Yu chose three thousand picked horse and pursued him to exhaustion; by night they reached Sandou Valley south of Jianwei, several li from the enemy; he waited until dawn to strike and took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Miwu slipped away; Yu chased with three thousand riders to Sandou south of Jianwei, camped within sight, and waited for daylight without posting guards.

sentences.zh: 迷吾乃伏兵三百人，夜突育营。

translations.literal: Miwu then laid an ambush of three hundred men who stormed Yu's camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: Miwu sprang three hundred men on the Han camp after dark.

sentences.zh: 营中惊坏散走，育下马手战，杀十余人而死，死者八百八十人。

translations.literal: The camp panicked; men scattered and fled; Yu dismounted and fought hand to hand; he slew over ten men then died; eight hundred eighty died.
translations.idiomatic: Panic emptied the camp; Yu died sword in hand after killing a dozen foemen; eight hundred eighty fell with him.

sentences.zh: 及诸郡兵到，羌遂引去。

translations.literal: When the various commandery troops arrived the Qiang then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements arrived too late; the Qiang had already melted away.

sentences.zh: 育，北地人也。

translations.literal: Yu was a man of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yu hailed from Beidi.

sentences.zh: 显宗初，为临羌长，与捕虏将军马武等击羌滇吾，功冠诸军；

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming's early reign he was chief of Linqiang and joined Capturing-Barbarians General Ma Wu and others in striking Dianwu of the Qiang; his merit topped every army.
translations.idiomatic: As Linqiang chief under Ming he rode with Ma Wu against Dianwu and earned first honors.

sentences.zh: 及在武威，威声闻于匈奴。

translations.literal: When he was in Wuwei his prestige reached the ears of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: His name crossed the steppe while he held Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 食禄数十年，秩奉尽赡给知友，妻子不免操井臼。

translations.literal: For decades on salary he gave every grain of his stipend to friends and acquaintances; his wife and children could not escape grinding grain at mortar and pestle.
translations.idiomatic: He fed friends out of his pay for years while his household still turned the quern.

sentences.zh: 肃宗下诏追褒美之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhang issued an edict posthumously praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang honored him by decree after death.

sentences.zh: 封其子毅为明进侯，七百户。

translations.literal: His son Yi was enfeoffed as marquis of Mingjin with seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yi received Mingjin marquisate at seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 以陇西太守张纡代为校尉，将万人屯临羌。

translations.literal: Longxi Governor Zhang Xu succeeded as colonel with ten thousand men garrisoned at Linqiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xu of Longxi replaced him with ten thousand men at Linqiang.

sentences.zh: 迷吾既杀傅育，狃忕边利。

translations.literal: After Miwu had killed Fu Yu he grew accustomed to profiting from the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Having killed Yu, Miwu learned how lucrative raiding could be.

sentences.zh: 章和元年，复与诸种步骑七千人入金城塞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhanghe he again joined various strains with seven thousand foot and horse entering the Jincheng barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanghe 1 he brought seven thousand fighters through Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 张纡遣从事司马防将千余骑及金城兵会战于木乘谷，迷吾兵败走，因译使欲降，纡纳之。

translations.literal: Zhang Xu sent aide Sima Fang with over a thousand horse and Jincheng troops to join battle at Mushang Valley; Miwu's army was defeated and fled; through interpreters he wished to surrender and Xu accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Xu sent Fang to Mushang; Miwu broke and sued for peace through translators; Xu agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂将种人诣临羌县，纡设兵大会，施毒酒中，羌饮醉，纡因自击，伏兵起，诛杀酋豪八百余人。

translations.literal: He then led tribesmen to Linqiang County; Xu arrayed troops at a great assembly and put poison in the wine; when the Qiang drank drunk Xu personally struck; ambush troops rose and executed over eight hundred chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: At Linqiang Xu poisoned the banquet liquor, then slaughtered above eight hundred chiefs when they collapsed.

sentences.zh: 斩迷吾等五人头，以祭育冢。

translations.literal: He beheaded five persons including Miwu and offered them at Yu's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Five heads, Miwu's among them, adorned Yu's grave.

sentences.zh: 复放兵击在山谷间者，斩首四百余人，得生口二千余人。

translations.literal: He again unleashed troops against those in mountain valleys, taking over four hundred heads and two thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: His men hunted the valleys for four hundred kills and two thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 迷吾子迷唐及其种人向塞号哭，与烧何、当煎、当阗等相结，以子女及金银娉纳诸种，解仇交质，将五千人寇陇西塞，太守寇盱与战于白石，迷唐不利，引还大、小榆谷，北招属国诸胡，会集附落，种众炽盛，张纡不能讨。

translations.literal: Mitang son of Miwu and his tribesmen wailed toward the barrier and allied with Shaohe, Dangjian, Dangtian, and others, using children and gold and silver as bride-price among strains, breaking old feuds and exchanging hostages; with five thousand men they raided Longxi barrier; Governor Kou Xu fought them at Baishi to Mitang's disadvantage; he withdrew to Great and Small Elm Valley, summoned dependent-state Hu northward, gathered dependent camps, and his tribes swelled until Zhang Xu could not suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang cried defiance, bought allies with gold and kin, struck Longxi, fell back to the Elm valleys, rallied Hu dependents, and grew too strong for Xu.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，纡坐征，以张掖太守邓训代为校尉，稍以赏赂离间之，由是诸种少解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan Xu was summoned for fault; Zhangye Governor Deng Xun replaced him as colonel and gradually used gifts to sow discord so the strains loosened somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Yongyuan 1 replaced Xu with Deng Xun, who bought splits among the tribes.

sentences.zh: 东吾子东号立。

translations.literal: Dongwu's son Donghao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Donghao followed Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 是时，号吾将其种人降。

translations.literal: At that time Haowu led his tribesmen in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Haowu brought his band to capitulate.

sentences.zh: 校尉邓训遣兵击迷唐，迷唐去大、小榆谷，徙居颇岩谷。

translations.literal: Colonel Deng Xun sent troops against Mitang; Mitang left Great and Small Elm Valley and moved to Poyan Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Xun attacked Mitang, who quit the Elm valleys for Poyan.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元四年，训病卒，蜀郡太守聂尚代为校尉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongyuan of Emperor He, Xun died of illness; Shu Governor Nie Shang succeeded as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: He Yongyuan 4 Xun died; Nie Shang of Shu took the colonelcy.

sentences.zh: 尚见前人累征不克，欲以文德服之，乃遣驿使招呼迷唐，使还居大、小榆谷。

translations.literal: Shang saw predecessors repeatedly campaign without success and wished to win them with civil virtue; he therefore sent relay riders to summon Mitang to return and dwell in Great and Small Elm Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Shang tried soft power: couriers invited Mitang home to the Elm valleys.

sentences.zh: 迷唐既还，遣祖母卑缺诣尚，尚自送至塞下，为设祖道，令译田汜等五人护送至庐落。

translations.literal: After Mitang returned he sent grandmother Beique to Shang; Shang personally escorted her below the barrier, held a farewell ritual for travelers, and ordered interpreters Tian Si and five others to convoy her to the camps.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang sent his grandmother; Shang saw her to the pass with ceremony and five escorts.

sentences.zh: 迷唐因而反叛，遂与诸种共生屠裂汜等，以血盟诅，复寇金城塞。

translations.literal: Mitang therefore rebelled; together with various strains they butchered and dismembered Si and the others, swore alliance with blood, and again raided Jincheng barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang repaid kindness by executing the escorts in a blood oath and hitting Jincheng again.

sentences.zh: 五年，尚坐征免，居延都尉贯友代为校尉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shang was summoned for fault and dismissed; Yanqi Commandant Guan You replaced him as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5 cashiered Shang; Guan You of Yanqi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 友以迷唐难用德怀，终于叛乱，乃遣驿使构离诸种，诱以财货，由是解散。

translations.literal: You saw Mitang could not be moved by virtue of cherishing and ended in rebellion; he therefore sent relay riders to estrange the strains and tempted them with wealth and goods; thereby they scattered.
translations.idiomatic: You bought defections with cash after deciding virtue had failed.

sentences.zh: 友乃遣兵出塞，攻迷唐于大、小榆谷，获首虏八百余人，收麦数万斛，遂夹逢留大河筑城坞，作大航，造河桥，欲度兵击迷唐。

translations.literal: You then sent troops beyond the pass and attacked Mitang in Great and Small Elm Valley, gaining over eight hundred heads and heads of captives, harvesting tens of thousands of hu of wheat; he then built fortress enclosures along both banks of the Fengliu Great River, constructed great ferry boats, and built a bridge over the river intending to cross troops and strike Mitang.
translations.idiomatic: You struck the Elm valleys, seized grain, walled Fengliu, bridged the river, and prepared another thrust.

sentences.zh: 迷唐乃率部落远依赐支河曲。

translations.literal: Mitang then led tribes far off to rely on the bend of the Zhizhi River.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang fled to the Zhizhi bend.

sentences.zh: 至八年，友病卒，汉阳太守史充代为校尉。

translations.literal: Down to the eighth year You died of illness; Hanyang Governor Shi Chong succeeded as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Year 8 You died; Shi Chong of Hanyang replaced him.

sentences.zh: 充至，遂发湟中羌胡出塞击迷唐，而羌迎败充兵，杀数百人。

translations.literal: When Chong arrived he immediately mobilized Zhong-loop Qiang and Hu beyond the pass against Mitang; the Qiang met and defeated Chong's troops, killing several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Chong rashly marched Zhong allies out and lost hundreds.

sentences.zh: 明年，充坐征，代郡太守吴祉代为校尉。

translations.literal: The next year Chong was summoned for fault; Dai Governor Wu Zhi succeeded as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Chong fell; Wu Zhi of Dai took over.

sentences.zh: 其秋，迷唐率八千人寇陇西，杀数百人，乘胜深入，胁塞内诸种羌共为寇盗，众羌复悉与相应，合步骑三万人，击破陇西兵，杀大夏长。

translations.literal: That autumn Mitang led eight thousand men against Longxi, killing several hundred; riding victory he pressed deep and coerced Qiang strains inside the barrier into joint banditry; the mass of Qiang again all responded; combining foot and horse thirty thousand they defeated Longxi troops and slew the chief of Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: That fall Mitang swept Longxi with eight thousand, snowballed to thirty thousand inside and out, and killed Daxia's magistrate.

sentences.zh: 遣行征西将军刘尚、越骑校尉赵代副，将北军五营、黎阳、雍营、三辅积射及边兵羌胡三万人讨之。

translations.literal: It dispatched Acting General Campaigning West Liu Shang with Zhao Dai vice-commander of the Imperial Household Rapid-as-Horses leading Northern Army five camps, Liyang, Yong camp, capital-region crossbowmen and frontier troops of Qiang and Hu thirty thousand to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Shang and Zhao Dai with thirty thousand regulars and tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 尚屯狄道，代屯枹罕。

translations.literal: Shang camped at Didao; Dai camped at Fuhan.
translations.idiomatic: Shang held Didao; Dai Fuhan.

sentences.zh: 尚遣司马寇盱监诸郡兵，四面并会。

translations.literal: Shang sent Major Kou Xu to supervise commandery troops converging from four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ordered Kou Xu to coordinate the surrounding columns.

sentences.zh: 迷唐惧，弃老弱，奔入临洮南。

translations.literal: Mitang feared, abandoned old and weak, and fled into Lintao south.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang bolted south of Lintao, leaving elders behind.

sentences.zh: 尚等追至高山。

translations.literal: Shang and others pursued to high mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Han host chased him into the heights.

sentences.zh: 迷唐穷迫，率其精强大战。

translations.literal: Mitang cornered led his crack troops in great battle.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped, Mitang turned with his best warriors.

sentences.zh: 盱斩虏千余人，得牛马羊万余头。

translations.literal: Xu beheaded over a thousand enemies and took over ten thousand head of cattle, horses, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Xu counted a thousand kills and myriad livestock.

sentences.zh: 迷唐引去。

translations.literal: Mitang withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang broke contact.

sentences.zh: 汉兵死伤亦多，不能复追，乃还入塞。

translations.literal: Han troops also suffered many dead and wounded and could not pursue further; they therefore returned inside the barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Han losses barred further pursuit; they fell back within the wall.

sentences.zh: 明年，尚、代并坐畏懦征下狱，免。

translations.literal: The next year Shang and Dai were both summoned for cowardice and cast into prison; dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Both generals went to jail for timidity.

sentences.zh: 谒者王信领尚营屯枹罕，谒者耿谭领代营屯白石。

translations.literal: Herald Wang Xin commanded Shang's camp at Fuhan; Herald Geng Tan commanded Dai's camp at Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin held Fuhan; Geng Tan Baishi.

sentences.zh: 谭乃设购赏，诸种颇来内附。

translations.literal: Tan then set rewards for capture; various strains came to attach within in considerable numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Tan offered bribes; tribes drifted inward.

sentences.zh: 迷唐恐，乃请降。

translations.literal: Mitang feared and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang offered to yield.

sentences.zh: 信、谭遂受降罢兵，遣迷唐诣阙。

translations.literal: Xin and Tan then accepted surrender and stood down troops, sending Mitang to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The heralds took his capitulation and escorted him toward court.

sentences.zh: 其余种人不满二千，饥窘不立，入居金城。

translations.literal: The remaining tribesmen numbered fewer than two thousand; starving and desperate they could not sustain themselves and entered to dwell in Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under two thousand hungry followers crossed into Jincheng.

sentences.zh: 和帝令迷唐将其种人还大、小榆谷。

translations.literal: Emperor He ordered Mitang to lead his tribesmen back to Great and Small Elm Valley.
translations.idiomatic: He Di told Mitang to repatriate the Elm valleys.

sentences.zh: 迷唐以为汉作河桥，兵来无常，故地不可复居，辞以种人饥饿，不肯远出。

translations.literal: Mitang thought Han had built the river bridge so troops could come unpredictably; therefore old lands could not be dwelt in again; he pleaded tribesmen hunger and refused to go far out.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang cited Han's bridge and famine to refuse the move.

sentences.zh: 吴祉等乃多赐迷唐金、帛，令籴谷市畜，促使出塞，种人更怀猜惊。

translations.literal: Wu Zhi and others therefore generously gifted Mitang gold and silk, ordering him to buy grain and market livestock, urging him beyond the pass; tribesmen grew more suspicious and frightened.
translations.idiomatic: Officials showered gold to coax him out; his people only grew jumpier.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遂复背叛，乃胁将湟中诸胡，寇抄而去。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they therefore rebelled again; coercing Zhong-loop Hu they raided and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years on he rebelled again, dragging Zhong Hu into the raid.

sentences.zh: 王信、耿谭、吴祉皆坐征，以酒泉太守周鲔代为校尉。

translations.literal: Wang Xin, Geng Tan, and Wu Zhi were all summoned for fault; Jiuquan Governor Zhou Wei replaced him as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: All three commanders fell; Zhou Wei of Jiuquan became colonel.

sentences.zh: 明年，迷唐复还赐支河曲。

translations.literal: The next year Mitang returned again to the Zhizhi bend.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Mitang was back at Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 初，累姐种附汉，迷唐怨之，遂击杀其酋豪，由是与诸种为仇，党援益疏。

translations.literal: At first the Lejie strain attached to Han; Mitang resented them and therefore attacked and killed their chieftains; thereby he became enemy to various strains and partisan aid grew ever thinner.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered Lejie chiefs who had sided with Han, isolating himself.

sentences.zh: 其秋，迷唐复将兵向塞，周鲔与金城太守侯霸，及诸郡兵、属国湟中月氏诸胡、陇西牢姐羌，合三万人，出塞至允川，与迷唐战。

translations.literal: That autumn Mitang again led troops toward the barrier; Zhou Wei with Jincheng Governor Hou Ba and commandery troops, dependent-state Yuezhi Hu of Zhong and Longxi Laojie Qiang combined thirty thousand and went beyond the pass to Yunchuan to battle Mitang.
translations.idiomatic: That fall Wei, Ba, Yuezhi Hu, and Laojie mustered thirty thousand at Yunchuan.

sentences.zh: 周鲔还营自守，唯侯霸兵陷阵，斩首四百余级。

translations.literal: Zhou Wei returned to camp and held defensive posture alone; only Hou Ba's troops pierced the lines and took over four hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Wei hugged his tents while Ba charged for four hundred kills.

sentences.zh: 羌众折伤，种人瓦解，降者六千余口，分徙汉阳、安定、陇西。

translations.literal: Qiang masses were broken and wounded; tribesmen scattered and dissolved; those surrendering numbered over six thousand mouths and were separately moved to Hanyang, Anding, and Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand surrendered and were resettled across three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 迷唐遂弱，其种众不满千人，远逾赐支河首，依发羌居。

translations.literal: Mitang then weakened; his tribes numbered fewer than a thousand; he crossed far beyond the Zhizhi headwaters and lodged with the Fa Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Mitang shrank below a thousand and clung to Fa Qiang beyond the river's source.

sentences.zh: 明年，周鲔坐畏懦征，侯霸代为校尉。

translations.literal: The next year Zhou Wei was summoned for cowardice; Hou Ba succeeded as colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei fell for cowardice; Ba replaced him.

sentences.zh: 安定降羌烧何种胁诸羌数百人反叛，郡兵击灭之，悉没入弱口为奴婢。

translations.literal: Surrendered Qiang of Anding of the Shaohe strain coerced several hundred Qiang of various strains into rebellion; commandery troops attacked and extinguished them; all weak mouths were confiscated as slaves and maids.
translations.idiomatic: Anding Shaohe rebels were crushed and survivors enslaved.

sentences.zh: 时，西海及大、小榆谷左右无复羌寇。

translations.literal: At that time west of the Western Sea and around Great and Small Elm Valley there were no further Qiang raids.
translations.idiomatic: For a moment the Western Sea and Elm country stayed quiet.

sentences.zh: 隃麋相曹凤上言：“西戎为害，?世所患，臣不能纪古，且以近事言之。

translations.literal: Yu Prefecture Chancellor Cao Feng submitted: "The western Rong doing harm has been a calamity successive ages worry over; your servant cannot narrate antiquity and will speak from recent matters.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Feng of Yu memorialized that western foes had plagued dynasty after dynasty.

sentences.zh: 自建武以来，其犯法者，常从烧当种起。

translations.literal: Since Jianwu those who broke the law have constantly begun from the Shaodang strain.
translations.idiomatic: Since Guangwu's restoration every major rising started with Shaodang.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，以其居大、小榆谷，土地肥美，又近塞内，诸种易以为非，难以攻伐。

translations.literal: The reason they are thus is that they dwell in Great and Small Elm Valley where land is fertile and fat and they are also near inside the barrier; various strains easily join them in wrongdoing and they are hard to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Their Elm valley seat was rich, close to the wall, and easy to rally.

sentences.zh: 南得钟存以广其众，北阻大河因以为固，又有西海鱼盐之利，缘山滨水，以广田蓄，故能强大，常雄诸种，恃其权勇，招诱羌胡。

translations.literal: Southward they obtained Zhongcun to enlarge their masses; northward they were blocked by the great river and relied on it as fortification; moreover they had profit from Western Sea fish and salt; along mountains bordering water they enlarged fields and herds; therefore they could become strong, constantly dominate various strains, rely on their power and bravery, and entice Qiang and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Fish, salt, rivers, and Zhongcun neighbors made them the swaggering magnet of the plateau.

sentences.zh: 今者衰困，党援坏沮，亲属离叛，余胜兵者不过数百，亡逃栖窜，远依发羌。
