translations.idiomatic: The throne taxed surrogates, tapped noble rents, and emptied vaults of coin, silk, grain, and iron.

sentences.zh: 所以赂遗购赏，转输劳来之费，前后数十巨万。

translations.literal: Thus bribes, rewards, transport, and relief expenses front and back ran to several tens of giant ten-thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts and convoys stacked into the billions.

sentences.zh: 或枭克酋健，摧破附落，降俘载路，牛羊满山。

translations.literal: Sometimes they beheaded stalwart chiefs, shattered dependent camps, filled roads with captives, and covered hills with cattle and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Victories piled heads, prisoners, and livestock.

sentences.zh: 军书未奏其利害，而离叛之状已言矣。

translations.literal: Before memorials gauged profit and harm reports already spoke of fresh rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatches barely praised gains before new defections arrived.

sentences.zh: 故得不酬失，功不半劳。

translations.literal: Therefore gains did not repay losses; achievements matched not half the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Every win cost more than it returned.

sentences.zh: 暴露师徒，连年而无所胜。

translations.literal: Armies lay exposed year after year yet achieved no lasting victory.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns dragged without decisive triumph.

sentences.zh: 官人屈竭，烈士愤丧。

translations.literal: Officials were drained and stalwart hearts despaired.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaustion gripped court and camp.

sentences.zh: 段颎受事，专掌军任，资山西之猛性，练戎俗之态情，穷武思尽飙锐以事之。

translations.literal: Duan Jiong took office monopolizing military charge, drawing on western hill fierceness, drilling Rong customs' temper, exhausting martial thought and lightning vigor to serve the task.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong poured frontier ruthlessness into total war.

sentences.zh: 被羽前登，身当百死之阵；

translations.literal: Feathered pennants led the ascent; his body met formations of hundred deaths;
translations.idiomatic: He pressed forward under feathered pennants and threw himself into formations where death came a hundred ways.

sentences.zh: 蒙没冰雪，经履千折之道。

translations.literal: He braved snow and ice treading thousand-bend roads.
translations.idiomatic: He endured snow and ice along passes that bent a thousand times.

sentences.zh: 始殄西种，卒定东寇。

translations.literal: He first exterminated western strains and finally settled eastern raiders.
translations.idiomatic: He finished the western tribes before pinning the eastern.

sentences.zh: 若乃陷击之所歼伤，追走之所崩籍，头颅断落于万丈之山，支革判解于重崖之上，不可校计。

translations.literal: As for those smashed in assaults and trampled in pursuits—heads fell from towering cliffs and limbs split on layered ravines—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Assault and pursuit littered gorges with heads and limbs beyond tally.

sentences.zh: 其能穿窜草石，自脱于锋镞者，百不一二。

translations.literal: Those who could pierce grass and rock to escape arrows numbered not one or two in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than one in a hundred slipped through the net.

sentences.zh: 而张奂盛称“戎狄一气所生，不宜诛尽，流血污野，伤和致妖”。

translations.literal: Yet Zhang Huan loudly declared 'Rong and Di are born of single qi; it is not fitting to slaughter to the end; blood staining the wilds wounds harmony and summons prodigies.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huan preached mercy—that steppe peoples shared one breath with Han.

sentences.zh: 是何言之迂乎！

translations.literal: How pedantic those words!
translations.idiomatic: How pedantic!

sentences.zh: 羌虽外患，实深内疾，若攻之不根，是养疾疴于心腹也。

translations.literal: Although Qiang are an outer peril they are truly a deep inner sickness; if you strike without rooting them out you nurture disease in the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang unrest was an internal ulcer pretending to be a border itch.

sentences.zh: 惜哉寇敌略定矣，而汉祚亦衰焉。

translations.literal: Alas—the raiders were nearly pacified yet Han fortune also declined.
translations.idiomatic: The foe ebbed even as dynastic pulse faded.

sentences.zh: 呜呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 昔先王疆理九土，判别畿荒，知夷貊殊性，难以道御，故斥远诉华，薄其贡职，唯与辞要而已。

translations.literal: Ancient kings mapped nine soils and distinguished capital from wilds, knowing Yi and Mo differed in nature and could hardly be guided by the Way; therefore they pushed them far from Hua, lightened tribute duties, and dealt only in words and covenants.
translations.idiomatic: The sages kept barbarians at arm's length with token tribute.

sentences.zh: 若二汉御戎之方，失其本矣。

translations.literal: As for the two Han methods of managing Rong they missed that root.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern and Western Han forgot that lesson.

sentences.zh: 何则？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 先零侵境，赵充国迁之内地；

translations.literal: Xianling violated the border and Zhao Chongguo moved them into inner lands;
translations.idiomatic: When Xianling raided the frontier, Zhao Chongguo resettled them deep inside Han territory.

sentences.zh: 煎当作寇，马文渊徙之三辅。

translations.literal: Dangjian acted as bandits and Ma Yuan relocated them to Three Assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuan parked Dangjian bands near the capital.

sentences.zh: 贪其暂安之势，信其驯服之情，计日用之权宜，忘经世之远略，岂夫识微者之为乎？

translations.literal: Greedy for momentary calm, trusting their tame appearance, reckoning day-to-day expedients, they forgot long-range planning for the age—was this the deed of one who reads subtle signs?
translations.idiomatic: They traded durable peace for a quiet afternoon and mistook temporary tameness for lasting submission—was that the judgment of men who read the signs?

sentences.zh: 故微子垂泣于象箸，辛有浩叹于伊川也。

translations.literal: Therefore Weizi wept over ivory chopsticks and Xin You sighed at the Yi River.
translations.idiomatic: So Weizi mourned delicate chopsticks and Xin You foresaw disaster at Yichuan.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：金行气刚，播生西羌。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Metal phase's qi is hard; it spreads life to western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The verse praises Metal-born hardness in western Qiang.

sentences.zh: 氐豪分种，遂用殷强。

translations.literal: Di chiefs split strains and thereby grew mighty.
translations.idiomatic: Di magnates multiplied branches into strength.

sentences.zh: 虔刘陇北，假僭泾阳。

translations.literal: They ravaged Long north and usurped titles along the Jing.
translations.idiomatic: They wasted Long's north and crowned kings by the Jing valleys.

sentences.zh: 朝劳内谋，兵惫外攘。

translations.literal: The court wore itself plotting within while troops tired beating them without.
translations.idiomatic: Han plotted itself weary turning outer raids.
